title: Design System: La Yeguada OBC — Chatbot Admin

2xs.purpose: Smallest step: stat labels, table headers, timestamps, avatar initials, footer text.

xs.purpose: Tags, status badges, field labels, secondary chrome.

sm.purpose: Table cells, chat bubbles, page subtitles.

base.purpose: Default: buttons, inputs, nav items, panel titles.

data.purpose: Any live-changing number: counts, percentages, scores, timestamps.

shadows.name: md
shadows.purpose: Mobile sidebar/chat drawers when floating over content.

shadows.name: focus
shadows.purpose: Focus ring on inputs, tinted from the accent.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions and drawer slides.

narrative.overview:
This dashboard exists so a small, non-technical community organization can trust and operate an AI system they didn't build. The rejected default was the generic AI-dashboard template it started as: a green gradient topbar, circular avatar bubbles, unicode-glyph icons, pill badges on every element, and same-size hero-metric cards with a decorative top accent bar and a faint background emoji.

The rebuilt system reads instead as calibrated equipment: a single unified stat strip instead of four separate cards, hairline 1px dividers instead of shadows, monospace figures for anything measured, and one committed accent color used sparingly rather than a five-color nature palette scattered across badges. The register is explicitly the one the user asked for — Linear, Stripe, and Vercel's dashboards — translated through La Yeguada's own single accent rather than a generic SaaS blue.
keyCharacteristics: One committed accent (deep forest green) on an otherwise fully neutral, cool-gray system
Monospace for every measured figure; proportional sans for everything else
Hairline (1px) structure over shadow — elevation is rare and reserved for overlays
Small, precise radii (6–10px); never a pill except true status chips
A unified stat strip replaces the four-identical-KPI-card template

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Only one saturated color exists in this system. If a new state needs a color, reach for a neutral or a semantic (warning/danger) before introducing a second accent hue.

rules.name: The Measured-Figure Rule
rules.body: Any number that represents a live measurement (a count, a percentage, a score, a duration, a timestamp) is set in the mono face with tabular figures. Static prose numbers stay in the UI face.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A panel at rest never has a shadow. Shadow only appears on a surface that is temporarily floating above the rest of the page (a drawer, a tooltip).

rules.name: The Six-Step Rule
rules.body: Every font-size is one of six scale steps (2xs/xs/sm/base/heading/data). A one-off literal size is a bug, not a variant — snap it to the nearest step or add a new named step, never both an old and a near-duplicate new value.

dos: Do set every live-measured number in JetBrains Mono with tabular figures.
Do use hairline 1px borders as the default structural device; reach for shadow only on genuinely floating surfaces.
Do keep the accent to a small minority of any screen — active state, primary action, resolved status, one chart series.
Do author icons as single-stroke SVG at a consistent 1.75px weight; never fall back to emoji or unicode glyphs.
Do use the stat-strip pattern (bordered row + internal dividers) for any new grouped-metrics display, not a grid of separate cards.
donts: Don't introduce a second saturated accent color; route new states through the neutral scale or the warning/danger semantics.
Don't use a full pill radius on anything except true status chips and the segmented control.
Don't add a decorative top accent bar, background icon glyph, or gradient fill to a card.
Don't animate width/height/padding/margin for data-driven bars — animate transform: scaleX() from a transform-origin instead.
Don't use a colored border-left above 1px as a generic emphasis device.
